source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
Skybox Houston One sits on 96,129 square feet of technical space in Harris County, Texas. The operator has not published a megawatt figure for IT load or critical power on the facility page this site read, so no rack or accelerator estimate can be derived. Without a power number, the campus cannot be ranked among the 13 Texas facilities that have published capacity figures, and it falls outside the 389 MW of published Texas capacity this site has tallied.

The single published certification is LEED, which addresses the building's environmental and energy-efficiency design standards. LEED does not certify uptime tier, redundancy architecture, or suitability for any particular workload class. No Tier classification, SOC attestation, or other operational certification is listed in the published specifications.

Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities, of which only 13 have published a megawatt figure to this site. Skybox Houston One is one of the 120 facilities in the state for which no power figure is publicly available here. That gap is common across the state and reflects operator disclosure choices rather than facility size. Whether this campus carries AI workloads, and at what density, cannot be determined from what the operator has published.
